title: Nuclear power - Wikipedia
snippet: Nuclear power is the use of nuclear reactions to produce electricity. Nuclear power can be obtained from nuclear fission, nuclear decay and nuclear fusion reactions. Presently, the vast majority of electricity from nuclear power is produced by nuclear fission of uranium and plutonium in nuclear power plants.

title: What is Nuclear Energy? The Science of Nuclear Power
snippet: Nuclear energy is a form of energy released from the nucleus, the core of atoms, made up of protons and neutrons. This source of energy can be produced in two ways: fission - when nuclei of atoms split into several parts - or fusion - when nuclei fuse together. title: Nuclear energy | Definition, Sources, Uses, & Facts | Britannica
snippet: Nuclear energy, energy that is released in significant amounts in processes that affect atomic nuclei, the dense cores of atoms. One method of releasing nuclear energy is by controlled nuclear fission, used in nuclear power plants around the world. Another method, controlled nuclear fusion, has not yet been perfected.

title: Nuclear Energy - Education
snippet: Nuclear energy is the energy in the nucleus, or core, of an atom. Nuclear energy can be used to create electricity, but it must first be released from the atom.
